summary: Jürgen Neuß works in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin between circa 2002 and 2007, studying under Harry Falk.

Jürgen Renn is a historian and philosopher who studied at the Free University of Berlin (circa 1975–1983) and Technische Universität Berlin (circa 1983–1987). He held posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (circa 1994–2023), Free University of Berlin (circa 1995), and Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1998).

K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He served as a professor at the University of Lucknow (circa 1921–1957) and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (circa 1960–1966), teaching Dwijendra Nath Shukla.
K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer worked in Indology. He served as Managing Editor of the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras in 1927 and as Secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute in 1945.

K. Kunjunni Raja was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja (PhD), and the University of London under John Brough (PhD). His posts included Reader In-Charge at the University of Madras (circa 1958–1969), research fellow at the Calgary Institute for the Humanities (circa 1980–1981), and Research Committee Chairman at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (2001).

K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under Madhukar Anant Mehendale by 1964. She later held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University until 1983.

K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who taught Hugo David, Steven Edward Lindquist, and Mattia Salvini. He held academic posts as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

K. T. S. Sarao is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Panjab University, the University of Delhi (BA, MA, MPhil, PhD), and the University of Cambridge (PhD). He taught history at Kirori Mal College (1981), became a professor at Delhi (1995), and was a Visiting Fellow at St Edmund's College, Cambridge (circa 2004–2005).

K. V. Ramesh worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director at the Archaeological Survey of India (circa 1966–1993) and as Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore (circa 1993).
K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar was an Indologist and historian. He served as Principal at Banaras Hindu University and Central Hindu College between circa 1935 and 1938.

K. V. Sarma was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Kerala (circa 1938–1942). He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (circa 1943–1951), University of Madras (1951–1962), and Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre (circa 1990–2005).

K. Venkata Ramanan was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, and at Visva-Bharati University under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He was a Visiting Scholar at Harvard-Yenching Institute (circa 1957–1959) and Professor of Philosophy at Visva-Bharati.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo. He held an assistant professor post at Rissho University.

Kaikyoku Watanabe was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Strasbourg (circa 1900–1912). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (circa 1911–1923), Toyo University (circa 1911–1926), and Taisho University (circa 1926–1933).

Kaiten Nukariya was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Ryodo Nukariya and attended Komazawa University, Sendan-Rin School, and Keio University. His posts included first president of Komazawa University (1919–1934), lecturer at Harvard University (1913), and roles at Soto-shu University, Tokyo Sotoshu Chugakurin, and Soto-shu Koto Chugakurin.

Kalu Rinpoche was a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Palpung Monastery and under gurus including Bokar Rinpoche, Drupon Norbu Dondrup, Khakyab Dorje, and Tai Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, later directing three-year retreats at Palpung (circa 1942–1955).

Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (circa 1951–1956) and was appointed professor at the University of Windsor circa 1969.

Kamala Tiyavanich is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cornell University (circa 1988–1993) under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg. She held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship at Cornell from 1993 to 1994.
Kamaleswar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and philosopher who taught Hugo David. He held academic posts at the University of Toronto (circa 1977–1979), Brown University, and the University of Bonn.

Kameshwar Nath Mishra works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He taught Barbra R. Clayton, Philippe Turenne, Andy Rotman, and Martin T. Adam, holding posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as a Visiting Research Scholar at the University of Marburg in 1993.
